sources.locator: Sections 1.2-1.8, 3.1-3.7, 4.1-4.6 (bodies, motion, transport, mass, force and Cauchy stress, momentum and angular momentum balances), Section 11.2 with Problem 11.5 (linearized elasticity and strain energy), Sections 12.1-12.3 with Problems 12.9 and 12.14 (fluid models and channel flows)

contents.name: Sections 1.2-1.6: continuous bodies, reference and current configurations, motion of a body
contents.support: Body data, reference placement and the field slots of the model follow this presentation with explicit dimensions.

contents.name: Section 1.8: extensive properties and their densities
contents.support: Density as mass per volume and mass as an integral over a subregion.

contents.name: Sections 3.1-3.3: motion, velocity field, velocity gradient
contents.support: The smooth motion and spatial velocity adopted by the kinematic postulate.

contents.name: Section 3.7: transport equations for integrals over moving regions
contents.support: The transport identity and the material derivative read in model terms.

contents.name: Section 4.2: conservation of mass and the local continuity equation
contents.support: Integral mass balance, its localization and the material form.

contents.name: Section 4.3: force, contact force and Cauchy's hypothesis
contents.support: Body forces and the traction description adopted by the postulate.

contents.name: Sections 4.4-4.5: Cauchy tetrahedron and existence of the stress tensor
contents.support: Existence of the representing matrix from the force balance, with the reversed-normal identity.

contents.name: Sections 4.4-4.6: balance of linear momentum and the field equations
contents.support: The local momentum equation from the integral balance.

contents.name: Section 4.5: balance of angular momentum and symmetry of the stress tensor
contents.support: The couple-free torque balance argument is absorbed into the symmetry step of this item.

contents.name: Section 11.2 and Problem 11.5: linearized elasticity, strain energy and positive definiteness
contents.support: The adopted isotropic constitutive law and its positivity hypotheses.

contents.name: Section 11.2: the isotropic linearized elastic field equations
contents.support: The displacement equation and the plane-wave dispersion relation of the model.

contents.name: Sections 12.1-12.3: inviscid and incompressible viscous fluid constitutive models
contents.support: The Newtonian and barotropic branches adopted by the postulate.

contents.name: Problems 12.9 and 12.14: channel flows of the incompressible viscous model
contents.support: Poiseuille and Couette profiles with the no-slip wall data, verified on explicit numbers.

contents.name: Section 12.3: inviscid incompressible fluid and simple exact solutions
contents.support: The steady shear class is absorbed into the periodic-cell example, which also classifies the viscous steady shears.

contents.name: Chapters 13 and later: thermoelasticity and coupled thermodynamic constitutive theory
contents.reason: The continuum page adopts only mechanical constitutive branches and excludes thermal coupling explicitly; thermodynamic constitutive theory belongs to a thermodynamics track that is not part of this batch, so these chapters are not harvested here.
